subject: general
question: The Supreme Court and High Courts have power to issue writs in the nature of habeas corpus, quo warranto, mandamus, certiorari, prohibition, etc., under ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Articles 32 and 226.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Constitution of India provides for the** writ jurisdiction** of the Supreme Court and High Courts under **Articles 32 and 226** respectively.
 
• A **writ** is a **formal written order** issued by a court to a person or entity, either to perform a specific act or to **refrain** from doing a particular act.
 
• The writs that can be issued by the** Supreme Court and High Courts** include habeas corpus, quo warranto, mandamus, certiorari, and prohibition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Habeas corpus** is a writ that can be used to** secure the release of a person **who has been unlawfully detained.
 
• **Quo warranto** is a writ that can be used to **challenge the authority of a person** holding public office.
 
• **Mandamus** is a writ that can be used to compel a public official or government agency to perform a **specific duty.**
 
• **Certiorari** is a writ that can be used to review the decision of a** lower court or tribunal.**
 
• **Prohibition** is a writ that can be used to **prevent a court or tribunal **from exceeding its jurisdiction.
